question.prompt:
Each of the small circles in the figure has radius one. The innermost circle is tangent to the six circles that surround it, and each of those circles is tangent to the large circle and to its small-circle neighbors. Find the area of the shaded region.

[Figure 1](figures/2002_AMC_12A_Q05_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The shaded region is the large disk with the seven unit disks removed, so finding the large radius is enough.

Let \(O\) be the innermost circle's center, and let \(P\) and \(R\) be the large circle's center and radius. Each surrounding circle is externally tangent to the innermost circle, so its center is \(1+1=2\) units from \(O\). Each is internally tangent to the large circle, so its center is \(R-1\) units from \(P\).

Consequently, the six surrounding centers lie both on a circle centered at \(O\) and on a circle centered at \(P\). Three distinct points on a circle are noncollinear, and their perpendicular bisectors meet at a unique circumcenter. Both \(O\) and \(P\) must be that circumcenter, so \(P=O\). Hence
\[
R-1=2,
\qquad R=3.
\]
The seven small disks have disjoint interiors, so their areas can all be subtracted once. The shaded area is
\[
\pi(3^2)-7\pi(1^2)
=9\pi-7\pi
=\boxed{2\pi}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutions.title: Find the large radius from the centers
